What Makes This Book Different

The conversation no one has been brave enough to write down.

Most personal finance books pretend the black tax does not exist. This one does not.

An entire chapter is dedicated to one of the hardest financial pressures in Ghanaian life. Not advice on how to refuse your family. Advice on how to give sustainably, with structure, with self-respect, and with the actual scripts for the hard conversations you have been avoiding.

Real People · Real Numbers

Real Ghanaians on real salaries.

Three case studies that prove what is possible.

The Teacher

Grace Pokuaa

A GES teacher in Koforidua earning GHS 3,200 a month. GHS 870 was quietly leaving her household every month in "small things" she never planned for. She found it, named it, and rebuilt her financial life one decision at a time.

The Nurse

Sister Patience

A nurse at Ridge Hospital. Bought her first plot of land in 2018 for GHS 35,000. By 2026, she earns GHS 38,400 a year in rental income from a property she built one stage at a time.

The Customs Officer

Stephen Mensah

Started in 2014 on a GHS 2,800 salary. Today, after 10 years of patient, unglamorous work, his net worth is GHS 1.2 million. He never inherited anything. He followed a plan.

You can be next.

About Emmanuel Adu-Gyamfi

Emmanuel Adu-Gyamfi spent fifteen years on a salary before he understood how wealth actually works. A former civil servant turned financial educator, he writes for the millions of people who were never taught what to do with a pay slip beyond spending it.

From Salary to Wealth is his first book.

The next ten years of your life are already being written.

The only question is whether you are writing them, or whether they are writing themselves.
